reasons: Tests were not run while writing these notes.
Coverage is broad, but the Windows-only test cannot run on other systems.

terms.meaning: a text-based drawing file format used by CAD programs
the zip-based format behind Word, Excel and PowerPoint files
a link inside an Office file that points to another internal part
a table where spreadsheets store repeated text once
a shortcut defined inside XML that can expand into text
a tagged text format used inside Office files
a connected line made of several points
the recorded outcome for each file

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for document tests
sections.what: Brings in the test tools, the archive checker, and the extraction functions for packages, drawings and Office files.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests cover several file types through the same entry points.

sections.name: office
sections.title: Builds a fake Office file
sections.what: Writes a zip container with the given internal parts to a file with the chosen extension, the way Word, Excel and PowerPoint files are built.
sections.why: Likely reason: Office files are zip containers, so tests can control their exact contents.

sections.name: workbook
sections.title: Builds a small spreadsheet
sections.what: Creates a workbook with one sheet holding the given cells, optionally marked as linking to an outside file.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets tests check cell handling and external link refusal without a real spreadsheet program.

sections.name: test_formula_cache_is_separate_missing_is_not_zero
sections.title: Formula results kept apart from stored values
sections.what: Checks that a formula cell keeps its formula and stored result, that an empty result is recorded as missing rather than zero, and that an error result is recorded as an error. None are marked as checked by calculation.
sections.why: Likely reason: a stored result may be stale, so the tool must not call it verified or turn missing into zero.
sections.watch_out: Treating a blank result as zero would put false numbers into the model.

sections.name: test_direct_extraction_and_atomic_receipts_handle_long_paths
sections.title: Long Windows folder paths work
sections.what: Runs the full extraction into a very long folder name and confirms it completes with no failures, a readable result file, and no leftover pending files.
sections.why: Likely reason: Windows limits path length, and temporary files must not be left behind.
sections.watch_out: This runs only on Windows, so path problems can go unnoticed elsewhere.

sections.name: test_external_worksheet_never_opened
sections.title: External workbook links never opened
sections.what: A workbook pointing to another file is refused with an External worksheet error, and the other file is not opened.
sections.why: Likely reason: opening outside files could expose data or run unexpected content.

sections.name: test_duplicate_or_invalid_cell_locators_fail
sections.title: Duplicate or invalid cell addresses fail
sections.what: Refuses a sheet with two cells at the same address, or an address containing path characters, with a cell coordinate error.
sections.why: Likely reason: an ambiguous address would make extracted values unreliable.

sections.name: test_docx_paragraph_and_table_locators
sections.title: Word paragraphs and tables get positions
sections.what: From a Word file with one paragraph and one table, checks the paragraph is numbered 1 with its text, the table row holds its cell text, and the page count is left unknown.
sections.why: Likely reason: page numbers are not stored in the file, so the tool reports unknown rather than guessing.

sections.name: test_xml_entities_are_never_expanded
sections.title: XML shortcuts never expanded
sections.what: A Word file whose XML defines a custom shortcut for text must raise an entities error and not expand it.
sections.why: Likely reason: expanding such shortcuts is a known attack that can exhaust memory.
sections.watch_out: The safe XML reader must stay in use, since a plain reader would expand these shortcuts.

sections.name: dxf
sections.title: Builds a fake drawing file
sections.what: Writes a small DXF text drawing with an optional unit setting and the given entities.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets tests check drawing reading without a CAD program.

sections.name: test_dxf_units_and_planar_z_not_invented
sections.title: Drawing units and flat height not invented
sections.what: For drawing unit codes that are missing, zero, two or six, reads a line whose end points are flat at height zero. The declared unit is reported exactly, and the status says undeclared for missing or zero and declared otherwise. A burial depth limitation note is kept.
sections.why: Likely reason: a drawing does not say its unit or height unless declared, so the tool must not guess.

sections.name: test_invalid_dxf_coordinates_fail
sections.title: Bad drawing numbers fail
sections.what: A point with a coordinate of NaN, infinity, or a huge number raises a coordinate error.
sections.why: Likely reason: such values would corrupt positions in the model.

sections.name: test_unsupported_dxf_entity_keeps_accountability
sections.title: Unknown drawing items still listed
sections.what: An unknown block insert is listed as unsupported with no geometry, so every drawing item is accounted for.
sections.why: Likely reason: a reviewer should see everything in the drawing, even what cannot be drawn.

sections.name: test_every_reference_has_truthful_disposition
sections.title: Every file gets an honest outcome
sections.what: Runs extraction on a package with two drawings, a hidden temporary file, a lock file and a broken Word file. Confirms the walk finished but not all supported content was processed. Counts two unsupported, two auxiliary, and one failed, and the failure is listed as a core failure.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the summary never claims success for skipped or broken files.
sections.watch_out: The complete flag means the walk finished, not that everything was understood, so it must not be read as success.

sections.name: test_auxiliary_alias_cannot_hide_supported_content
sections.title: Helper file names cannot hide real content
sections.what: With a Word file and a helper file of the same content, in either order, the real document is extracted once with its text kept in its detail file, and the helper is counted as not interpreted.
sections.why: Likely reason: the order of files in a package should not change what is read.

sections.name: test_wrong_office_root_is_failed_not_empty_success
sections.title: Wrong spreadsheet structure is a failure
sections.what: A workbook whose main part has the wrong top tag raises a Workbook part error rather than returning empty results.
sections.why: Likely reason: an empty success would hide a broken file.

sections.name: test_duplicate_office_relationship_ids_rejected
sections.title: Duplicate internal link ids refused
sections.what: A Word file with two internal links sharing one id raises a duplicate relationship error.
sections.why: Likely reason: the id is used to find targets, so a duplicate would make the target ambiguous.

sections.name: test_old_dxf_polylines_retain_vertex_identity
sections.title: Old polyline vertices keep their identity
sections.what: An old style polyline with two vertices yields one parent line with both points and lists the two vertices as children, each marked as part of a supported polyline.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps vertices linked to their parent instead of duplicating geometry.

sections.name: test_dxf_conflicting_units_and_blocks_remain_visible
sections.title: Conflicting drawing units and blocks stay visible
sections.what: A drawing declaring two different units is marked conflicted with no declared unit, both unit claims are kept, and a block definition is marked unsupported.
sections.why: Likely reason: a conflicting unit must not be quietly picked.

sections.name: test_polyline_child_transform_cannot_be_promoted
sections.title: Polyline vertex transform not promoted
sections.what: A polyline vertex carrying an extra transform gets no geometry for the parent, and the vertex is marked unsupported with a transform note.
sections.why: Likely reason: applying that transform would be guessing, so the tool refuses.

sections.name: test_wrong_shared_string_root_rejected
sections.title: Wrong shared text table refused
sections.what: A workbook whose shared text table has the wrong top tag raises a shared-string error.
sections.why: Likely reason: cell text comes from that table, so a wrong one means the values cannot be trusted.

sections.name: test_word_orphan_header_is_not_document_evidence
sections.title: Unlinked Word headers are not content
sections.what: A header part counts as extracted only when the document references it. Otherwise it is marked unreferenced and its text is left out.
sections.why: Likely reason: unlinked headers may be leftovers, so they should not count as document content.

sections.name: test_absolute_slide_target_and_duplicate_identity
sections.title: Slide links and duplicate slide ids checked
sections.what: A presentation with an absolute slide target extracts one slide. The same slide id used twice raises a duplicate slide error.
sections.why: Likely reason: duplicate slide ids would make slide identity ambiguous.

sections.name: test_oversized_content_failure_reaches_reference_dispositions
sections.title: Oversized files still reported
sections.what: With a lowered size cap, a large Word file fails while a helper file is recorded as not interpreted, and the counts reflect both outcomes.
sections.why: Likely reason: an oversized file must still appear in the accounting.

sections.name: test_report_publication_retries_only_bounded_sharing_failures
sections.title: Report writing retries only sharing locks
sections.what: Writing the final report retries when Windows file sharing blocks it, up to a set number of tries. A few failures are overcome; too many raise the error, leave the earlier report unchanged, and leave no pending files.
sections.why: Likely reason: antivirus or another program can briefly lock files on Windows.
sections.watch_out: The retry limit is checked by this test, so changing it means updating the test.

summary: Tests how the app reads Word, Excel, PowerPoint and CAD drawing files, and how it reports anything it could not read.
purpose: Confirms that text and drawing content is read accurately, that risky input is refused, and that every file gets an honest outcome.
why: Likely reason: documents in a package vary widely and can be broken or hostile, so each case is pinned down. Reason not stated in the code beyond this.
how: Each test builds a small Office or DXF file with the helpers, runs an extraction function, and checks the returned content, the outcome labels, or the expected error. Some tests run the full package extraction and read its saved results.
inputs: Hand-built Office and DXF files, zip packages, and per-test limit overrides.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest, plus temporary extraction results read by the tests.
risks: The Windows long-path test runs only on Windows, so path problems may go unnoticed elsewhere. Several checks rely on exact error wording.
debug: Start with the failing test name. Check the outcome labels it compares and the saved extraction file in the temporary folder.
